entries.name: self-propbytes-overlong-constants-count-accept#0
entries.description: An overlong VLQ for the constants count (`81 00` for 1, `83 00` for 3): the same count in two bytes instead of one, so the kept span is one byte LONGER than the writer's form. The script compares the first 3 bytes of `SELF.propositionBytes` against `108300` — the encoding AS RECEIVED — and the spend is VALID. The spent box is PARSED from bytes, so its tree keeps this span (ErgoTreeSerializer.scala:178-185) and its id is over it. An implementation that re-writes the tree on parse reads the writer's form instead and answers the opposite way.

entries.name: self-propbytes-overlong-constants-count-rewritten-reject#1
entries.description: The reject twin: the same shape, with the script expecting `100304` — the bytes the WRITER gives back for the same tree. The JVM reads the span it parsed, the comparison is false and the spend is INVALID. **SEPARATING:** an implementation that re-writes the tree on parse compares its own output, finds it equal, and ACCEPTS. The spent box is PARSED from bytes, so its tree keeps this span (ErgoTreeSerializer.scala:178-185) and its id is over it. An implementation that re-writes the tree on parse reads the writer's form instead and answers the opposite way.

expected.reason: org.ergoplatform.validation.MalformedModifierError: Scripts of all transaction inputs should pass verification. 6fed6ac01a19580722fd0f5541112ba25e46422793f51fefe150c660df665c66: #0 => Success((false,6))

entries.name: self-propbytes-overlong-constants-count-canonical-control-reject#2
entries.description: **CONTROL** for the accept arm: the SAME script (it expects `108300`) spent over the CANONICAL encoding of itself, `1003040004060e03108300d193b4c2a7730073017302`. The window now holds the writer's bytes, so the comparison is false and the spend is INVALID. It is what shows the accept arm reads the tree's own encoding rather than a constant that happens to match.

entries.name: self-propbytes-declared-size-over-accept#10
entries.description: A size-flagged tree whose declared size is one byte TOO LARGE. The parse does not use the declared size to bound the span it keeps — it keeps `r.position - startPos`, the bytes the root actually consumed — so the tree parses and the kept bytes carry the wrong size byte. The script compares the first 2 bytes of `SELF.propositionBytes` against `1815` — the encoding AS RECEIVED — and the spend is VALID. The spent box is PARSED from bytes, so its tree keeps this span (ErgoTreeSerializer.scala:178-185) and its id is over it. An implementation that re-writes the tree on parse reads the writer's form instead and answers the opposite way.

entries.name: self-propbytes-last-byte-trueleaf-accept#30
entries.description: `7f` is `TrueLeaf`, which the parser accepts and the writer NEVER emits — it writes the Boolean constant `0101` instead. So this is the one direction where a re-writing implementation reads MORE bytes than the JVM kept: the kept span is one byte SHORTER. The script reads the LAST byte of `SELF.propositionBytes` (which needs no fixed point on the length: each implementation indexes its own last byte) and requires `7f`: VALID. The spent box is PARSED from bytes, so its tree keeps this span (ErgoTreeSerializer.scala:178-185) and its id is over it. An implementation that re-writes the tree on parse reads the writer's form instead and answers the opposite way.

entries.name: self-propbytes-last-byte-trueleaf-rewritten-reject#31
entries.description: The reject twin, reached without changing the script: the SAME script spent over the CANONICAL encoding `00d1ed93b2c2a799b1c2a7040200027f0101`, whose last byte is `01` (the Boolean constant's value byte). The comparison is false and the spend is INVALID. **SEPARATING:** an implementation that re-writes reads `01` for BOTH encodings, so it rejects the accept arm above and accepts nothing here — it is red on the pair, not on one row.

expected.reason: org.ergoplatform.validation.MalformedModifierError: Scripts of all transaction inputs should pass verification. 713a92e6a43aaa59a23db18afbc33b108c5e0cfa1ff31005423a2bfcf405b79e: #0 => Success((false,14))

entries.name: self-propbytes-last-byte-falseleaf-accept#40
entries.description: The second lengthening form, which the probe did not ask for: `80` is `FalseLeaf`, written back as `0100`. The proposition is `check || false` so that a FalseLeaf can sit LAST in the body without making the script false. The script requires the last byte to be `80` (-128 as a signed byte): VALID. The spent box is PARSED from bytes, so its tree keeps this span (ErgoTreeSerializer.scala:178-185) and its id is over it. An implementation that re-writes the tree on parse reads the writer's form instead and answers the opposite way.

entries.name: self-propbytes-last-byte-falseleaf-rewritten-reject#41
entries.description: Its twin over the canonical encoding, whose last byte is `00`: INVALID. **SEPARATING** the same way as the TrueLeaf pair, and together they say the class has two members rather than one.
